verdict.rationale: Unreal's first-party Blueprints Visual Scripting system lets designers use "virtually the full range of concepts and tools generally only available to programmers". The Remote Control docs also confirm that functions can be "defined and implemented entirely in Blueprint". Community users confirm Blueprints are used in practice, but note they are best for prototyping and get inefficient at high complexity, and some tasks still push users to C++. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of gameplay-logic node coverage, and evidence that complex gameplay systems can be built without falling back to C++.

support.subject: As a technical artist, I can build gameplay logic with visual scripting without writing code
